name: Éomer, King of Rohan
oracle_text:
Double strike
Éomer enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each other Human you control.
When Éomer enters, target player becomes the monarch. Éomer deals damage equal to its power to any target.
blocked_sentences: Éomer enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each other Human you control.
When Éomer enters, target player becomes the monarch. Éomer deals damage equal to its power to any target.

needs.what: `ReplacementModel.amount` must accept a *value expression* from `value_keys`, not just a literal integer, so `self_enters_with_counters` can say "a +1/+1 counter for each other Human you control" -- here `{"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Human"], "exclude_self": true}}`. The evaluation site already has everything it needs: `zones.py:302-304` evaluates the replacement's `condition` with `controller=obj.controller, source=obj.oid` on the board the permanent is arriving on, so the same call shape evaluates an amount. The change is `amount: int = 1` -> `amount: int | dict[str, Any] = 1` in `schema.py:231`, a `validate_value` pass beside the existing `validate_condition` in `loader.py:270-276`, and evaluating it instead of `int(replacement.get("amount", 1))` at `zones.py:324-326`. This is a large family, not one card: `data/authoring/queue.json` holds 25+ cards deferred with "no template for: ... enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each ..." (each other creature you control, each Gate you control, each creature that died this turn, each color of mana spent to cast it / Converge, each Zombie card in your graveyard, other Kithkin, Ulasht, Verazol), and every one of them is unblocked by this single field widening.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The `replacements` mechanism itself exists and is the right home -- `self_enters_with_counters` is what Mossborn Hydra uses for its fixed "enters with a +1/+1 counter on it" and what `_replacements_with_loyalty` compiles a planeswalker's starting loyalty into -- but `amount` is typed `int = 1` in `schema.py:231` under a `Strict` model config, so a value expression is a validation error and only a constant can be printed. The nearest substitute is a `self_enters` triggered ability running `add_counters` with the count as its `amount`, and it is wrong three ways on this card in particular. (1) It is a trigger, not a replacement: Éomer is on the battlefield as a 2/2 first and grows later, whereas 614.1c/121.6 mean he is never seen without the counters. (2) The second printed line deals damage *equal to Éomer's power*, so the substitute makes the card's whole payload depend on which of two simultaneous enters triggers the controller happens to order first -- 2 damage or 2+N, from a card whose printed text has no such choice in it. (3) The op route fires COUNTER_PLACED (`primitives.py:313-321`) while the replacement route calls `obj.add_counter` directly and fires nothing (`zones.py:319-326`), so the substitute would additionally wake up every `counter_placed` watcher on the board. `add_counters` inside the trigger cannot be made to behave like a replacement, and there is no other slot in `ops` for an as-enters modification.

needs.what: The monarch designation as game state: at most one player is the monarch at a time, that player draws a card at the beginning of their end step, and a player becomes the monarch whenever a creature they control deals combat damage to the monarch. Needs the designation stored on GameState (a player id or None) and both automatic behaviours wired into the end step and the combat damage step. Éomer is the first card in the family that can hand the designation to *an opponent* on purpose, so the exclusivity rule is load-bearing rather than incidental: giving it away must take it off whoever held it, and the end-step draw must follow it. A `condition_keys` entry (`is_monarch`, taking a player selector) is not needed by Éomer itself but is by the rest of the family, so it belongs in the same piece of work.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `set_flag`/`has_flag` is the nearest thing in `reference` and only stores an opaque per-card boolean: `has_flag` is read off the source object rather than a player, it is not exclusive across players, nothing moves it when a creature deals combat damage to its holder, and no end-step draw hangs off it -- so a card written on flags would print "target player becomes the monarch" and deliver none of what monarch means. `has_city_s_blessing` is the right *shape* (a per-player boolean) but is one-way and non-exclusive by design, the opposite of a designation exactly one player holds and that moves between them. `docs/rules-coverage.md:242-244` records the monarch and the initiative as not implemented; nothing in `src/` matches /monarch/. Already requested by `aragorn_king_of_gondor`, `champions_of_minas_tirith`, `crown_of_gondor`, `faramir_steward_of_gondor`, `forth_eorlingas`, `oath_of_eorl` and `palace_jailer` -- same engine need, listed again so this card is linked to it.

needs.what: An op that makes a player the monarch -- `become_monarch` -- taking a **player selector**, not a hardcoded "you". Every monarch card requested so far reads "you become the monarch"; Éomer reads "*target player* becomes the monarch", which is the first use that must resolve against a chosen player and must therefore accept a `player` target from the card's `targets` list (the `player` selector key and the player-quantifier machinery already exist, per `tests/unit/test_player_quantifier.py`). If the op is built with an implicit "you", Éomer stays blocked after the rest of the family ships, so the selector belongs in the op from the start.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: No op in `ops` grants a player-level designation. `set_flag` is the closest and writes a card-scoped flag with no game-wide meaning; there is no monarch state for any op to set until the engine need above lands. `for_each_player` iterates players but has nothing to do to them here.

closest_existing: self_enters_with_counters replacement with a literal amount (Mossborn Hydra, planeswalker loyalty)
count value key over a subtypes/exclude_self selector
rest_is_expressible: Line 1 is done already -- `double_strike` is a known keyword and is in the packet's `starting_point`. The second half of line 3 is also expressible on its own: `damage` with `amount: {"power_of": {"self_only": true, "zone": "battlefield"}}` and an any-target spec is ordinary DSL. Nothing was written as an answer, because neither remaining printed line can be claimed in full. Line 2's counter amount is variable and the replacement slot only takes a constant, and there is no honest constant to pick -- "for each other Human you control" is 0 in the sandbox position and unbounded in play. Line 3 is one printed sentence containing the monarch clause and the damage clause, so an ability claiming it would have to either implement half of it (the residual gate reads an ability's `text` as the whole line it claims) or drop the monarch clause silently. Both are the substituted-nearby-op failure the brief forbids, and dropping the monarch is not cosmetic here: it is a repeatable card-a-turn engine and the reason Éomer is a five-mana 2/2 body rather than a rate-appropriate creature.
